- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply smoothing or lagged decay to correct for momentum bias.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to recognize it; add a 1-2 day lagged mean reversion buffer.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be too optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5-7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; dampen initial forecast slope.
- When sentiment history shows repeated volatility (e.g., alternating +0.5 and -0.3), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted moving average to stabilize forecast.
- If true outcome deviates >10% from model in first 5 days, check sentiment for “panic” or “fear” signals (e.g., -0.6+), and adjust downward by 5-10% to reflect behavioral correction.
